Subject: SLA request: multi-region failover RTO/RPO for Acme Platform

Hi Hannah,

Thanks for the demo earlier — Acme's platform team reviewed Redwood's HA/DR story and we have a specific request tied to our compliance posture and customer SLAs. We're looking to include explicit multi-region failover commitments in our contract amendment. High level asks: 

- Active-active cross-region failover for our production model endpoints (primary region: us-west-2, failover region: us-east-1)
- Recovery Time Objective (RTO) <= 5 minutes
- Recovery Point Objective (RPO) <= 30 seconds (we cannot accept > 1 minute for certain streams)
- Capacity reservation for sustained QPS peaks up to 5x baseline during failover window
- Regular DR runbook reviews and an annual DR exercise with results shared
- Financial credits for failures exceeding agreed SLOs and an escalation path to on-call support (24/7)

We know these are more prescriptive than the standard hosted API terms. We're happy to consider Dedicated or a hybrid private topology if that is required. We're targeting procurement sign-off in the next 6 weeks and will need a redline and a proposed amendment draft to review. 

Attached: ACME_DR_requirements.xlsx (high-level RTO/RPO matrix + traffic profile).

Can you confirm whether Redwood can commit to these thresholds (or provide alternative commitments + mitigations)? If this needs escalation, please loop in whoever is needed.

Thanks,
Nancy

Hi Nancy — thanks again for the detailed ask and for giving us time to pull the team together. Below is a summary of the proposed amendment we can put in a draft for procurement review. This is intended to balance your RTO/RPO needs with operational guarantees we can reasonably deliver.

Proposed (for Dedicated with reserved capacity and active-active replication):
- Committed RTO: 10 minutes for full failover initiation and traffic cutover (detection and automatic routing change).
- Committed RPO: <= 60 seconds for model state and request-level durability (we will provide specific replication windows per endpoint).
- Capacity Reservation: Dedicated reserved pool sized at X vGPU units to cover baseline + 5x burst for 30 minutes. Overage billing or temporary scale-up options will be included.
- DR Exercises: Quarterly smoke tests and an annual full DR exercise with joint runbook validation.
- Credits: Tiered SLA credit schedule tied to total time outside the committed RTO/RPO; standard cumulative cap equal to up to 12 weeks of service credits per year for repeated failures (detailed schedule to be drafted by Legal).
- Escalation: 24/7 priority on-call for active incident management during failover events.

Notes and mitigations:
- The stricter numbers you requested (RTO <= 5m / RPO <= 30s) are technically feasible for some endpoints under very specific conditions (fully pinned Dedicated capacity, synchronous replication for stateful artifacts, and a joint acceptance test). We recommend designating a small set of critical endpoints for a validated "Gold" tier if you need 5m/30s guarantees. That would require an additional reserved-capacity premium and a 4-6 week ops readiness validation.
- For Hosted (non-dedicated) customers we can offer an operational best-effort multi-region failover with RTO <= 15 minutes and RPO <= 2 minutes, but this would not be contractually guaranteed.

Next steps: 
1) If this aligns, I'll generate a draft amendment (proposed_sla_template.docx) with draft credit language and capacity reservation clauses and send to procurement/legal.
2) Schedule a 45-minute technical run-through with your SREs and our infra team (Marcus and Monica suggested availability next Tue/Thu).
3) If you want 5m/30s for a set of endpoints, nominate them and we'll scope the Gold tier and pricing.

Sound reasonable? If so I'll put together the amendment and start the DocuSign flow.

Best,
